🔻 Iran exercised its right to self-defense against aggression: Deputy FM

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs Kazem Gharibabadi has emphasized that the Iranian nation exercised its natural right to self-defense against aggression to its territories and national interest.

Speaking at the 31st Conference of the States Parties to the Chemical Weapons Convention in the Hague on Monday, Gharibabadi said, “We did not welcome war. We did not start this war. But when our territory, our people, and our national interests were subjected to aggression, the Iranian nation exercised its natural right to self-defense.”
​
He added, “Iran seeks peace, but peace born of surrender is not peace. Peace founded on threats is not peace. From this podium, we declare: Iran does not seek war, but neither will it embrace a peace that sacrifices the independence of the Iranian nation.”
​
“Iran’s history carries a clear message: the Iranian nation cannot be brought to its knees through threats,” Gharibabadi noted.
​
The full text of his speech is as follows:
​
At the outset, I wish to congratulate you on your election as President of the Thirty-First Conference of the States Parties to the Chemical Weapons Convention and wish you every success in guiding the work of this Conference. I also congratulate the newly appointed Director-General of the Organization, Ms. Sabrina Dallafiore Matera, and wish her every success in discharging her responsibilities. Furthermore, I wish to express the support of the delegation of the Islamic Republic of Iran for the statement delivered by Bangladesh on behalf of the Asian Group.
​
The Islamic Republic of Iran, as one of the largest and last victims of the widespread use of chemical weapons in contemporary history, continues to confront a bitter and enduring reality—one whose consequences remain evident, even after decades, in the lives of thousands of Iranian citizens. Many of these victims continue to suffer from the physical and psychological effects of exposure to these inhumane weapons and require life-saving medicines, continuous care and specialized medical treatment in order to sustain their lives.
​
For the Iranian nation, chemical weapons are not merely a historical subject or an abstract issue within the framework of disarmament. They are part of the collective memory and lived experience of a people who have endured their inhumane consequences with their very bodies and souls.
​
Despite that painful experience, the Islamic Republic of Iran never resorted to the logic of retaliatory use of chemical weapons. Despite the capability and the opportunity to respond in kind during the imposed war waged by Saddam’s regime, Iran never chose to produce or use such weapons. It believed that responding to a crime must not lead to the repetition of that same crime. This decision stemmed from a sense of responsibility, adherence to humanitarian principles and the moral superiority of a nation that had itself fallen victim to these weapons. This historical experience makes Iran’s principled position clear: chemical weapons are inhumane and unacceptable, regardless of who uses them or against whom they are used, and their use can under no circumstances be justified.
​
Fundamentally, from our perspective, one of the important indicators of strength lies in the actions and measures that a State has the capability to undertake, but deliberately refrains from taking.
